name: File System Access: folder picker and blocked folders
plain: Lets the person grant a whole folder for reading and writing; sensitive system folders are refused.
meaning: A folder grant shares every file inside it and lets the site edit them. Chrome refuses root, system and the profile home folders so one click cannot expose the whole disk.

access.prompt_ui: Chrome folder picker, then View files and Save changes bubbles
access.persistence: Handle storable in IndexedDB; permission per session or persistent in Chrome 122
access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
access.iframe: Not in cross-origin iframes; secure context
steps: Chrome shows folder picker and View files confirmation
Page walks the tree through the handle

limits.headline: Can open and change files in a whole folder you pick, but not system folders
limits.user_action: You click Open folder, choose a folder, then click Allow.
can: List every file and subfolder inside the folder
Save changes and create new files in it, after you allow saving
Keep access on later visits if you choose Allow on every visit
cannot: See anything outside the folder you picked
Pick sensitive folders, such as system folders or your whole home folder
Save changes before you allow the Save changes prompt
limits.differs: Chrome and Edge on computers only. Firefox, Safari and phones do not have it.

story.what_it_is: Lets you give a site read and write access to a whole folder. Sensitive system folders are refused.

marketing.name: File System Access API
marketing.pitch: Google pitches it as a way for web apps to read and save files and folders like native apps.

story.for_you: A system window asks you to pick a folder. A second prompt asks 'Let this site edit files in this folder?' Allow it and the site can change files until you stop it.
story.for_makers: It lets web editors and tools work like desktop software on real folders. That wins users from native apps. Browsers block folders like Documents and Downloads roots to keep people safe.

use_cases.example: A web code editor opens your whole project folder and saves changes in place.
A photo or music tool works on a folder of your files and saves edits back.
A browser game level editor reads and writes your whole mod folder.
A note taking web app keeps your notes as plain files in a folder you own.
A web tool builds a site into a folder on your computer.
A scam site asks to edit a folder to plant or change files. Browsers refuse the system folders.

technical_bounds: Chrome 86 and later only; no Firefox, Safari

Blocked for selection (Chrome blocklist): the drive root, system folders such as Windows, Program Files, System and Library on macOS, /etc and /usr on Linux, and the user's whole home folder; its subfolders can usually be chosen
Two prompts: View files (read) and Save changes (write) when readwrite is requested
Cannot move above the chosen folder; no path strings are exposed (only names)
Large trees: values() iteration is async with no fixed cap; each entry needs permission checks
Folders with executables get an extra warning for writes

legit_uses: Code editors and static site tools
abuse: Copying a whole folder tree to a server

history.change: showDirectoryPicker ships with a path blocklist
